13:1.sourceText: Ἦσαν δὲ ἐν Ἀντιοχείᾳ κατὰ τὴν οὖσαν ἐκκλησίαν προφῆται καὶ διδάσκαλοι ὅ τε Βαρνάβας καὶ Συμεὼν ὁ καλούμενος Νίγερ, καὶ Λούκιος ὁ Κυρηναῖος, Μαναήν τε Ἡρῴδου τοῦ τετραάρχου σύντροφος καὶ Σαῦλος.
13:1.targetText: And there were certain in Antioch, in the assembly there, prophets and teachers: both Barnabas, and Simeon who is called Niger, and Lucius the Cyrenian, Manaen also—Herod the tetrarch’s foster-brother—and Saul;

groups.note: The actual Antioch name identifies the assembly’s place; English first names Antioch and then resumes that same locality with there. No independently printed Greek there adverb is invented.
The actual preposition is κατά with the existing assembly phrase, rendered in; the preceding in Antioch has its own actual ἐν.
The actual Κυρηναῖος is the ethnic/personal designation Cyrenian; both pinned analyses record N-NSM, a noun analysis, not an independently printed Cyrene place-name.

The actual σύντροφος is an adjective used of a person brought up with another, rendered foster-brother. No separate brother noun is printed. Primary lexical entry: https://www.billmounce.com/greek-dictionary/syntrophos .

unmappedSource.reason: The actual οὖσαν is a being/existing participle qualifying assembly, without a separately rendered English being word. The English location there is separately anchored to the actual Antioch name.
The article before Barnabas is not separately expressed.

unmappedTarget.reason: The pinned TR includes τινες, certain, absent from pinned N1904.

13:2.sourceText: Λειτουργούντων δὲ αὐτῶν τῷ Κυρίῳ καὶ νηστευόντων εἶπεν τὸ Πνεῦμα τὸ Ἅγιον Ἀφορίσατε δή μοι τὸν Βαρνάβαν καὶ Σαῦλον εἰς τὸ ἔργον ὃ προσκέκλημαι αὐτούς·
13:2.targetText: and in their ministering to the LORD and fasting, the Holy Spirit said, “Separate to Me both Barnabas and Saul to the work to which I have called them,”

groups.note: The actual genitive-absolute ministering participle supplies the circumstantial in ... ministering frame; no separate Greek in preposition is printed here.
The actual genitive αὐτῶν is the personal subject of the ministering/fasting construction, expressed as English possessive their.

The actual relative ὃ is accusative and resumes work in the calling clause. English renders the same work-goal relation as to which; no additional Greek to preposition is printed before this relative in either pinned N1904 or TR.

unmappedSource.reason: The repeated article before Holy and the article before Barnabas are not separately expressed.
The actual δή is an emphatic imperative particle, not separately expressed as now or indeed in English. It is not a both word.

unmappedTarget.reason: The pinned TR has an additional τε before the named pair, absent from pinned N1904.

13:3.sourceText: τότε νηστεύσαντες καὶ προσευξάμενοι καὶ ἐπιθέντες τὰς χεῖρας αὐτοῖς ἀπέλυσαν.
13:3.targetText: then having fasted, and having prayed, and having laid the hands on them, they sent [them] away.

groups.note: The actual dative αὐτοῖς is the same named pair receiving the hand-laying and being sent away in the immediate coordinated actions. English resumes them as the sending object; one actual pronoun is retained, not an invented additional source object.

13:4.sourceText: Αὐτοὶ μὲν οὖν ἐκπεμφθέντες ὑπὸ τοῦ Ἁγίου Πνεύματος κατῆλθον εἰς Σελεύκιαν, ἐκεῖθέν τε ἀπέπλευσαν εἰς Κύπρον,
13:4.targetText: These, indeed, then, having been sent forth by the Holy Spirit, went down to Seleucia, and from there they sailed to Cyprus,

groups.note: The actual αὐτοί is an emphatic personal pronoun for the named pair, rendered These; it is not a printed οὗτοι demonstrative.

13:5.sourceText: καὶ γενόμενοι ἐν Σαλαμῖνι κατήγγελλον τὸν λόγον τοῦ Θεοῦ ἐν ταῖς συναγωγαῖς τῶν Ἰουδαίων· εἶχον δὲ καὶ Ἰωάνην ὑπηρέτην.
13:5.targetText: and having come to Salamis, they declared the word of God in the synagogues of the Jews, and they also had John [as] a servant;

groups.note: The actual γενόμενοι is a becoming/being participle in an arrival-at-place construction, rendered having come; it is not a printed ἔρχομαι participle.
The actual ἐν gives location in Salamis; English uses directional to after its having-come rendering.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies the bracketed role marker as; the Greek directly adds the servant/helper complement without a comparison word.

13:6.sourceText: διελθόντες δὲ ὅλην τὴν νῆσον ἄχρι Πάφου εὗρον ἄνδρα τινὰ μάγον ψευδοπροφήτην Ἰουδαῖον ᾧ ὄνομα Βαριησοῦς,
13:6.targetText: and having gone through the island to Paphos, they found a certain magus, a false prophet, a Jew, whose name [is] Bar-Jesus;

groups.note: The actual ᾧ is a dative relative, to whom the name belongs; English whose recasts that same name-bearer as a genitive relative.

unmappedSource.reason: N1904 explicitly says whole, ὅλην, not expressed in this English sentence; the pinned TR lacks that qualifier.
N1904 explicitly includes the man noun ἄνδρα, absent from the pinned TR and not separately rendered beside the actual magus/false-prophet/Jew designations.

unmappedTarget.reason: The Greek relative-name clause is nominal, without a written be verb; English supplies bracketed is.

13:7.sourceText: ὃς ἦν σὺν τῷ ἀνθυπάτῳ Σεργίῳ Παύλῳ, ἀνδρὶ συνετῷ. οὗτος προσκαλεσάμενος Βαρνάβαν καὶ Σαῦλον ἐπεζήτησεν ἀκοῦσαι τὸν λόγον τοῦ Θεοῦ·
13:7.targetText: who was with the proconsul Sergius Paulus, an intelligent man; this one having called for Barnabas and Saul, desired to hear the word of God,

13:8.sourceText: ἀνθίστατο δὲ αὐτοῖς Ἐλύμας ὁ μάγος, οὕτως γὰρ μεθερμηνεύεται τὸ ὄνομα αὐτοῦ, ζητῶν διαστρέψαι τὸν ἀνθύπατον ἀπὸ τῆς πίστεως.
13:8.targetText: and there withstood them Elymas the magus—for so is his name interpreted—seeking to pervert the proconsul from the faith.

unmappedSource.reason: The article under his name is not separately expressed.

13:9.sourceText: Σαῦλος δέ, ὁ καὶ Παῦλος, πλησθεὶς Πνεύματος Ἁγίου ἀτενίσας εἰς αὐτὸν
13:9.targetText: And Saul—who also [is] Paul—having been filled with the Holy Spirit, and having looked steadfastly on him,

groups.note: The actual genitive Spirit noun gives the filling content, rendered with the Holy Spirit; no separately printed Greek with preposition or article is present there.

unmappedTarget.reason: The alternate-name construction has no written be verb; English supplies bracketed is.
The pinned TR has an additional καί before having looked steadfastly, absent from N1904.

13:10.sourceText: εἶπεν Ὦ πλήρης παντὸς δόλου καὶ πάσης ῥᾳδιουργίας, υἱὲ διαβόλου, ἐχθρὲ πάσης δικαιοσύνης, οὐ παύσῃ διαστρέφων τὰς ὁδοὺς τοῦ Κυρίου τὰς εὐθείας;
13:10.targetText: said, “O full of all guile, and all recklessness, son of a devil, enemy of all righteousness, will you not cease perverting the right ways of the LORD?

groups.note: The actual ῥᾳδιουργία noun includes reckless or unscrupulous conduct, rendered recklessness. Primary lexical entry specifically cites this verse: https://www.billmounce.com/greek-dictionary/rhadiourgia .

unmappedSource.reason: The repeated article introducing the right modifier is not separately expressed.

13:11.sourceText: καὶ νῦν ἰδοὺ χεὶρ Κυρίου ἐπὶ σέ, καὶ ἔσῃ τυφλὸς μὴ βλέπων τὸν ἥλιον ἄχρι καιροῦ. παραχρῆμα δὲ ἔπεσεν ἐπ’ αὐτὸν ἀχλὺς καὶ σκότος, καὶ περιάγων ἐζήτει χειραγωγούς.
13:11.targetText: And now, behold, a hand of the LORD [is] on you, and you will be blind, not seeing the sun for a season”; and instantly there fell on him a mist and darkness, and he, going around, was seeking some to lead [him] by the hand;

groups.note: The actual ἄχρι καιροῦ, until a time, marks a bounded duration; English renders the whole constituent for a season without a different Greek for preposition.

The actual αὐτόν is the man affected by the mist and darkness, who immediately seeks hand-leaders for himself. English resumes that same affected person as bracketed him with leading; no additional Greek pronoun is invented.
The actual χειραγωγούς is a plural hand-leader noun, expanded as some to lead by the hand. Its source remains the compound person noun, not independent some, leading, and hand words.

unmappedTarget.reason: The opening hand-on-you expression has no written finite be verb; English supplies bracketed is.

13:12.sourceText: τότε ἰδὼν ὁ ἀνθύπατος τὸ γεγονὸς ἐπίστευσεν, ἐκπλησσόμενος ἐπὶ τῇ διδαχῇ τοῦ Κυρίου.
13:12.targetText: then the proconsul having seen what has come to pass, believed, being astonished at the teaching of the LORD.

13:13.sourceText: Ἀναχθέντες δὲ ἀπὸ τῆς Πάφου οἱ περὶ Παῦλον ἦλθον εἰς Πέργην τῆς Παμφυλίας· Ἰωάνης δὲ ἀποχωρήσας ἀπ’ αὐτῶν ὑπέστρεψεν εἰς Ἱεροσόλυμα.
13:13.targetText: And those around Paul having set sail from Paphos, came to Perga of Pamphylia, and John having departed from them, turned back to Jerusalem,

groups.note: The actual passive ἀναχθέντες is from ἀνάγω in its maritime putting-to-sea sense, rendered having set sail; no separate sail noun or sailing verb is printed.

unmappedSource.reason: The article before Paphos is not separately expressed.

13:14.sourceText: Αὐτοὶ δὲ διελθόντες ἀπὸ τῆς Πέργης παρεγένοντο εἰς Ἀντιόχειαν τὴν Πισιδίαν, καὶ ἐλθόντες εἰς τὴν συναγωγὴν τῇ ἡμέρᾳ τῶν σαββάτων ἐκάθισαν.
13:14.targetText: and they having gone through from Perga, came to Antioch of Pisidia, and having gone into the synagogue on the day of the Sabbaths, they sat down,

groups.note: The actual article and Πισιδίαν are an accusative Pisidian qualifier; both pinned analyses give A-ASF for the territorial adjective. English recasts it as of Pisidia without an independently printed Greek Pisidia place-name or of preposition here.
The actual coming participle and εἰς into jointly express the English having gone into; no entered compound source verb is substituted.

unmappedSource.reason: The article before Perga is not separately expressed.

13:15.sourceText: μετὰ δὲ τὴν ἀνάγνωσιν τοῦ νόμου καὶ τῶν προφητῶν ἀπέστειλαν οἱ ἀρχισυνάγωγοι πρὸς αὐτοὺς λέγοντες Ἄνδρες ἀδελφοί, εἴ τίς ἐστιν ἐν ὑμῖν λόγος παρακλήσεως πρὸς τὸν λαόν, λέγετε.
13:15.targetText: and after the reading of the Law and of the Prophets, the chief men of the synagogue sent to them, saying, “Men, brothers, if there be a word in you of exhortation to the people—say on.”

groups.note: The actual ἀρχισυνάγωγοι is one plural synagogue-ruler compound noun, expanded chief men of the synagogue; chief, men, and synagogue are not independent Greek words here.
The actual indefinite τίς qualifies word, any or a word, expressed by English a; its source remains the indefinite qualifier rather than a Greek indefinite article.
The actual ἐστιν is present indicative, rendered existential there be in the English conditional frame; the source is not a Greek subjunctive form.

13:16.sourceText: ἀναστὰς δὲ Παῦλος καὶ κατασείσας τῇ χειρὶ εἶπεν Ἄνδρες Ἰσραηλεῖται καὶ οἱ φοβούμενοι τὸν Θεόν, ἀκούσατε.
13:16.targetText: And Paul having risen, and having beckoned with the hand, said, “Men, Israelites, and those fearing God, listen:

unmappedSource.reason: The article before God is not separately expressed.

13:17.sourceText: ὁ Θεὸς τοῦ λαοῦ τούτου Ἰσραὴλ ἐξελέξατο τοὺς πατέρας ἡμῶν, καὶ τὸν λαὸν ὕψωσεν ἐν τῇ παροικίᾳ ἐν γῇ Αἰγύπτου, καὶ μετὰ βραχίονος ὑψηλοῦ ἐξήγαγεν αὐτοὺς ἐξ αὐτῆς,
13:17.targetText: the God of this people Israel chose our fathers, and He exalted the people in their sojourning in the land of Egypt, and He brought them out of it with a high arm;

groups.note: The actual people exalted are the same people whose immediate sojourning is described; English resumes that same named group as their. No additional Greek possessive is printed with sojourning.

unmappedSource.reason: The articles in our fathers and their sojourning are not separately expressed.

13:18.sourceText: καί ὡς τεσσερακονταετῆ χρόνον ἐτροποφόρησεν αὐτοὺς ἐν τῇ ἐρήμῳ,
13:18.targetText: and about a period of forty years He endured their conduct in the wilderness,

groups.note: The actual τεσσερακονταετῆ is a single forty-year adjective modifying the time noun, rendered of forty years; no separate Greek forty numeral or years noun is printed inside this adjective.

The actual τροποφορέω is the conduct-bearing or putting-up-with verb, rendered endured ... conduct. It does not separately print a conduct noun. Primary lexical entry: https://www.billmounce.com/greek-dictionary/tropophoreo .
The actual accusative αὐτούς identifies the people borne with, recast as the possessor their of the English conduct expression; it is not a Greek genitive pronoun.

13:19.sourceText: καὶ καθελὼν ἔθνη ἑπτὰ ἐν γῇ Χανάαν κατεκληρονόμησεν τὴν γῆν αὐτῶν
13:19.targetText: and having destroyed seven nations in the land of Canaan, He divided their land to them by lot.

groups.note: The actual κατακληρονομέω is give as inheritance, expressed by English divided ... by lot as inheritance-allotment wording; pinned TR uses the different related compound κατακληροδοτέω. The N1904 lexical head is retained, without an independent dividing verb or lot noun. Primary source for the actual head: https://www.billmounce.com/greek-dictionary/katakleronomeo .
The actual genitive αὐτῶν owns the land of the seven nations just named, not the unprinted receiving people; English their preserves that distinct owner.

unmappedSource.reason: The article under their land is not separately expressed.

unmappedTarget.reason: The pinned TR has an additional αὐτοῖς inheritance-recipient pronoun, absent from pinned N1904. The actual genitive αὐτῶν instead owns the nations’ land and is not reassigned to the different recipient group.

13:20.sourceText: ὡς ἔτεσιν τετρακοσίοις καὶ πεντήκοντα. καὶ μετὰ ταῦτα ἔδωκεν κριτὰς ἕως Σαμουὴλ προφήτου.
13:20.targetText: And after these things, about four hundred and fifty years, He gave judges—until Samuel the prophet;

groups.note: In the pinned N1904 punctuation, the about-four-hundred-and-fifty-years expression comes before the sentence break and And after these things, following the inheritance statement. The pinned TR and displayed LSV place this duration after after-these-things with the judges statement. The same original words retain their exact 13:20 identities despite the changed clause attachment.

13:21.sourceText: κἀκεῖθεν ᾐτήσαντο βασιλέα, καὶ ἔδωκεν αὐτοῖς ὁ Θεὸς τὸν Σαοὺλ υἱὸν Κείς, ἄνδρα ἐκ φυλῆς Βενιαμείν, ἔτη τεσσεράκοντα·
13:21.targetText: and thereafter they asked for a king, and God gave to them Saul, son of Kish, a man of the tribe of Benjamin, for forty years;

groups.note: The actual κἀκεῖθεν contracts and-from-there, rendered temporally and thereafter; no separate Greek temporal thereafter word is printed.
The accusative years noun gives duration, rendered for forty years without a separately printed for preposition.

unmappedSource.reason: The articles before God and Saul are not separately expressed.

13:22.sourceText: καὶ μεταστήσας αὐτὸν ἤγειρεν τὸν Δαυεὶδ αὐτοῖς εἰς βασιλέα, ᾧ καὶ εἶπεν μαρτυρήσας Εὗρον Δαυεὶδ τὸν τοῦ Ἰεσσαί, ἄνδρα κατὰ τὴν καρδίαν μου, ὃς ποιήσει πάντα τὰ θελήματά μου.
13:22.targetText: and having removed him, He raised up to them David for king, to whom also having testified, He said, I found David, the [son] of Jesse, a man according to My heart, who will do all My will.

groups.note: The actual θελήματα is plural, wishes or wills, in both pinned readings; English uses the singular collective will for that same object, not a different singular source form.

unmappedSource.reason: The article before David and the articles under My heart/My will are not separately expressed.

unmappedTarget.reason: The Greek patronymic article/genitive expression leaves the personal head understood; English supplies bracketed son, without an independently printed υἱός noun.

13:23.sourceText: τούτου ὁ Θεὸς ἀπὸ τοῦ σπέρματος κατ’ ἐπαγγελίαν ἤγαγεν τῷ Ἰσραὴλ Σωτῆρα Ἰησοῦν,
13:23.targetText: Of this one’s seed, God, according to promise, raised to Israel a Savior—Jesus,

unmappedSource.reason: The articles before God and under this one’s seed are not separately expressed.
The pinned N1904 has ἤγαγεν, brought, from ἄγω; the pinned TR has ἤγειρεν, raised, from ἐγείρω, behind the English raised. These distinct predicates remain unpaired.

unmappedTarget.reason: The English follows the pinned TR raising verb rather than N1904 brought; no ἐγείρω lemma is invented for the actual ἄγω token.

13:24.sourceText: προκηρύξαντος Ἰωάνου πρὸ προσώπου τῆς εἰσόδου αὐτοῦ βάπτισμα μετανοίας παντὶ τῷ λαῷ Ἰσραήλ.
13:24.targetText: John having first preached, before His coming, an immersion of conversion to all the people of Israel;

groups.note: The actual προκηρύξαντος is a single prior-proclaiming participle, rendered having first preached; first is not an independent Greek adverb here.
The actual πρὸ προσώπου, before the face of, is the idiomatic before expression introducing the coming; face is not independently translated as a body part in this constituent.

unmappedSource.reason: The article under His coming is not separately expressed.

13:25.sourceText: ὡς δὲ ἐπλήρου Ἰωάνης τὸν δρόμον, ἔλεγεν Τί ἐμὲ ὑπονοεῖτε εἶναι, οὐκ εἰμὶ ἐγώ· ἀλλ’ ἰδοὺ ἔρχεται μετ’ ἐμὲ οὗ οὐκ εἰμὶ ἄξιος τὸ ὑπόδημα τῶν ποδῶν λῦσαι.
13:25.targetText: and as John was fulfilling the course, he said, Whom do you suppose I am? I am not [He], but behold, He comes after me, of whom I am not worthy to loose the sandal of [His] feet.

groups.note: The actual τί is neuter accusative what, while the pinned TR has masculine accusative τίνα, whom; English Whom follows that person-question wording. The shared interrogative head is retained without claiming a masculine source form.
The actual accusative ἐμέ is the personal subject of the being infinitive, rendered English I in the finite question complement.
The actual εἶναι is a present infinitive, rendered am as the English finite complement of suppose; it is not a Greek first-person indicative occurrence.

The actual genitive relative οὗ identifies the person whose sandal/feet are being discussed. English resumes that same owner as bracketed His in the immediate foot phrase; one actual relative identity is retained without an additional possessive source pronoun.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies the bracketed identity predicate in I am not He; no corresponding personal predicate pronoun is printed here.

13:26.sourceText: Ἄνδρες ἀδελφοί, υἱοὶ γένους Ἀβραὰμ καὶ οἱ ἐν ὑμῖν φοβούμενοι τὸν Θεόν, ἡμῖν ὁ λόγος τῆς σωτηρίας ταύτης ἐξαπεστάλη.
13:26.targetText: Men, brothers, sons of the race of Abraham, and those among you fearing God, to you was the word of this salvation sent,

unmappedSource.reason: The article before God is not separately expressed.
The actual ἡμῖν is first-person plural to us; the pinned TR has second-person plural ὑμῖν, to you, followed by English to you. The different recipients remain unpaired.

unmappedTarget.reason: The English follows the pinned TR second-person recipient where N1904 has first-person to us.

13:27.sourceText: οἱ γὰρ κατοικοῦντες ἐν Ἱερουσαλὴμ καὶ οἱ ἄρχοντες αὐτῶν τοῦτον ἀγνοήσαντες καὶ τὰς φωνὰς τῶν προφητῶν τὰς κατὰ πᾶν σάββατον ἀναγινωσκομένας κρίναντες ἐπλήρωσαν,
13:27.targetText: for those dwelling in Jerusalem, and their chiefs, having not known this One, also the voices of the Prophets, which are being read every Sabbath—having judged [Him]—fulfilled,

groups.note: The actual this-one demonstrative names the same person not recognized and immediately judged. English resumes that same actual person as bracketed Him; no additional object pronoun is invented.
The actual ἀγνοήσαντες is one not-knowing or failing-to-recognize verb, expanded having not known without a separately printed Greek negative.
The actual κατά with πᾶν forms the distributive every-Sabbath expression; English every condenses that preposition-plus-adjective relation.

unmappedSource.reason: The article under their chiefs is not separately expressed.

13:28.sourceText: καὶ μηδεμίαν αἰτίαν θανάτου εὑρόντες ᾐτήσαντο Πειλᾶτον ἀναιρεθῆναι αὐτόν·
13:28.targetText: and having found no cause of death, they asked of Pilate that He should be slain,

groups.note: The actual Pilate name is accusative, the person asked, rendered of Pilate in the English asking construction; it is not a Greek genitive name or separate of preposition.
The actual passive infinitive of killing is rendered as the finite that ... should be slain content clause; there is no independent Greek that conjunction or should modal here.

13:29.sourceText: ὡς δὲ ἐτέλεσαν πάντα τὰ περὶ αὐτοῦ γεγραμμένα, καθελόντες ἀπὸ τοῦ ξύλου ἔθηκαν εἰς μνημεῖον.
13:29.targetText: and when they fulfilled all the things written about Him, having taken [Him] down from the tree, they laid Him in a tomb;

groups.note: The actual neuter plural article substantivizes the written-about-Him content, rendered the things without an independently printed Greek thing noun.

The actual genitive αὐτοῦ names the person described by the writings and immediately taken down and laid in the tomb. English repeats Him as patient of the two immediate coordinated actions; one actual person identity remains, without additional Greek object pronouns or a change to the recorded genitive form.

13:30.sourceText: ὁ δὲ Θεὸς ἤγειρεν αὐτὸν ἐκ νεκρῶν·
13:30.targetText: and God raised Him out of the dead,

unmappedSource.reason: The article before God is not separately expressed.

13:31.sourceText: ὃς ὤφθη ἐπὶ ἡμέρας πλείους τοῖς συναναβᾶσιν αὐτῷ ἀπὸ τῆς Γαλιλαίας εἰς Ἰερουσαλήμ, οἵτινες νῦν εἰσιν μάρτυρες αὐτοῦ πρὸς τὸν λαόν.
13:31.targetText: and He was seen for many days of those who came up with Him from Galilee to Jerusalem, who are His witnesses to the people.

groups.note: The actual relative ὃς resumes the preceding raised person. English recasts that relative clause as coordinated and He; it is not a separately printed καί plus personal pronoun.
The actual dative article identifies those to whom the person appeared, rendered of those after was seen; the source case remains dative, not genitive.

unmappedSource.reason: The article before Galilee is not separately expressed.
The actual νῦν, now, is not separately rendered in English; the pinned TR lacks this adverb.

13:32.sourceText: καὶ ἡμεῖς ὑμᾶς εὐαγγελιζόμεθα τὴν πρὸς τοὺς πατέρας ἐπαγγελίαν γενομένην,
13:32.targetText: And we proclaim good news to you—that the promise made to the fathers,

groups.note: The actual ὑμᾶς is an accusative gospel-recipient complement, rendered to you without a separately printed to preposition.
The actual εὐαγγελιζόμεθα is a single good-news-proclaiming verb, rendered proclaim good news; news is not an independent source noun.
The actual γενομένην is a becoming/occurring participle qualifying the promise, rendered made; no printed giving or making verb is substituted.
The actual ὅτι introducing the completion clause begins Greek13:33 but is displayed in the English announcement at13:32; its original source reference is retained.

13:33.sourceText: ὅτι ταύτην ὁ Θεὸς ἐκπεπλήρωκεν τοῖς τέκνοις ἡμῶν ἀναστήσας Ἰησοῦν, ὡς καὶ ἐν τῷ ψαλμῷ γέγραπται τῷ δευτέρῳ Υἱός μου εἶ σύ, ἐγὼ σήμερον γεγέννηκά σε.
13:33.targetText: God has completed this in full to us their children, having raised up Jesus, as also in the second Psalm it has been written: You are My Son—I have begotten You today.

groups.note: The actual ἐκπεπλήρωκεν is a single completed/fulfilled compound verb, rendered has completed in full; full is not an independent source adjective.

unmappedSource.reason: The article before God and the repeated article introducing second are not separately expressed.

unmappedTarget.reason: The English follows the pinned TR to-us/their-children expression, not N1904 our children; no unlike recipient or possessor is reassigned.

13:34.sourceText: ὅτι δὲ ἀνέστησεν αὐτὸν ἐκ νεκρῶν μηκέτι μέλλοντα ὑποστρέφειν εἰς διαφθοράν, οὕτως εἴρηκεν ὅτι Δώσω ὑμῖν τὰ ὅσια Δαυεὶδ τὰ πιστά.
13:34.targetText: And that He raised Him up out of the dead, to no longer return to corruption, He has said this: I will give to You the holy [blessings] of David [that are] faithful;

groups.note: The actual prospective μέλλοντα and returning infinitive jointly give the English infinitival to return construction. The written modal is retained within this source constituent, without an independently translated about-to phrase.
The actual οὕτως is the adverb thus, rendered this in the English He has said this introduction; it is not a Greek demonstrative object pronoun.
The actual neuter plural ὅσια is substantival for holy things or benefits, rendered holy blessings. Its source stays the ὅσιος adjective, not an invented blessing noun.

unmappedSource.reason: The quotation-introducing ὅτι is not separately expressed before the direct speech.

unmappedTarget.reason: The faithful adjective has no written be verb; English supplies bracketed are in the relative modifier.

13:35.sourceText: διότι καὶ ἐν ἑτέρῳ λέγει Οὐ δώσεις τὸν Ὅσιόν σου ἰδεῖν διαφθοράν.
13:35.targetText: for what reason He also says in another [place]: You will not give Your Holy One to see corruption;

groups.note: The actual διότι is one reason connective, expanded for what reason; there is no independently printed Greek reason noun.
The actual dative ἑτέρῳ is substantival another, with the quotation location/head understood; English supplies place within this adjectival expression, not a separately printed τόπος noun.
The actual substantival adjective is ὅσιος, rendered Holy One; its head is not replaced by the different ἅγιος lemma.

unmappedSource.reason: The article under Your Holy One is not separately expressed.

13:36.sourceText: Δαυεὶδ μὲν γὰρ ἰδίᾳ γενεᾷ ὑπηρετήσας τῇ τοῦ Θεοῦ βουλῇ ἐκοιμήθη καὶ προσετέθη πρὸς τοὺς πατέρας αὐτοῦ καὶ εἶδεν διαφθοράν·
13:36.targetText: for David, indeed, having served his own generation by the will of God, fell asleep, and was added to his fathers, and saw corruption,

groups.note: The actual ἰδίᾳ is the own/one’s-own adjective, rendered his own without an independent possessive pronoun.
The actual ἐκοιμήθη is an aorist passive sleep predicate, rendered fell asleep; no Greek falling verb is printed, and the source passive form is retained.

unmappedSource.reason: The article under his fathers is not separately expressed.

13:37.sourceText: ὃν δὲ ὁ Θεὸς ἤγειρεν, οὐκ εἶδεν διαφθοράν.
13:37.targetText: but He whom God raised up, did not see corruption.

groups.note: The actual accusative relative ὃν identifies the raised person; English makes that same person both matrix He and relative whom in its clause recast, without an additional Greek personal pronoun.

unmappedSource.reason: The article before God is not separately expressed.

13:38.sourceText: γνωστὸν οὖν ἔστω ὑμῖν, ἄνδρες ἀδελφοί, ὅτι διὰ τούτου ὑμῖν ἄφεσις ἁμαρτιῶν καταγγέλλεται, καὶ ἀπὸ πάντων ὧν οὐκ ἠδυνήθητε ἐν νόμῳ Μωϋσέως δικαιωθῆναι,
13:38.targetText: Let it therefore be known to you, men, brothers, that the forgiveness of sins is declared to you through this One,

sourceMoved.reason: The actual coordinated from-all-things/under-the-Law/justifying complement closes Greek13:38 but begins displayed LSV13:39. All ten actual word identities retain their original13:38 references.

13:39.sourceText: ἐν τούτῳ πᾶς ὁ πιστεύων δικαιοῦται.
13:39.targetText: and from all things in the Law of Moses from which you were not able to be declared righteous, everyone who is believing in this One is declared righteous;

groups.note: The actual genitive relative ὧν resumes all things under the preceding ἀπό relation. English repeats that same relation as from which; there is no second printed ἀπό before the relative.
The actual passive infinitive δικαιωθῆναι is rendered to be declared righteous; declared and righteous are not separate Greek predicates.

13:40.sourceText: βλέπετε οὖν μὴ ἐπέλθῃ τὸ εἰρημένον ἐν τοῖς προφήταις
13:40.targetText: see, therefore, it may not come on you that has been spoken in the Prophets:

groups.note: The actual ἐπέλθῃ is an aorist subjunctive of come-upon, rendered it may come; its compound verb remains, while the additional TR explicit on-you complement is separately documented.

unmappedTarget.reason: The pinned TR explicitly adds ἐφ᾽ ὑμᾶς as the affected people, absent from N1904. No second-person object is invented for this N1904 prediction clause.

13:41.sourceText: Ἴδετε, οἱ καταφρονηταί, καὶ θαυμάσατε καὶ ἀφανίσθητε, ὅτι ἔργον ἐργάζομαι ἐγὼ ἐν ταῖς ἡμέραις ὑμῶν, ἔργον ὃ οὐ μὴ πιστεύσητε ἐάν τις ἐκδιηγῆται ὑμῖν.
13:41.targetText: See, you despisers, and wonder, and perish, because I work a work in your days, a work in which you may not believe, though anyone may declare [it] to you.”

groups.note: The actual article identifies the addressed despisers, rendered you with that person designation; no independent Greek you pronoun is printed here.

The actual accusative relative refers to the second written work and supplies the object of believing. The same immediately described work is the content declared in the conditional clause; English repeats that object as bracketed it. The in of in which is the English believing-complement recast, not a printed Greek in preposition.
The actual ἐάν is a conditional conjunction, rendered concessively as though in this English if-anyone-declares frame; no different Greek though conjunction is substituted.

unmappedSource.reason: The article under your days is not separately expressed.

13:42.sourceText: Ἐξιόντων δὲ αὐτῶν παρεκάλουν εἰς τὸ μεταξὺ σάββατον λαληθῆναι αὐτοῖς τὰ ῥήματα ταῦτα.
13:42.targetText: And having gone forth out of the synagogue of the Jews, the nations were calling on [them] that on the next Sabbath these sayings may be spoken to them,

groups.note: The actual ἐξιόντων is a present active genitive participle in the leaving genitive absolute; English having gone forth has a different perfective frame, not an aorist source form.

The actual genitive αὐτῶν is the leaving speakers’ subject, retained as the same departing speakers addressed by the immediate appeal. English supplies that known pair as bracketed them after calling on; its source remains the actual genitive pronoun, not an invented accusative. The TR instead explicitly names Jews in the leaving construction and adds nations/synagogue material; those different named expressions remain distinct gaps.

unmappedSource.reason: The article under these sayings is not separately expressed.

unmappedTarget.text: out of the synagogue of the Jews
unmappedTarget.reason: The pinned TR adds the synagogue phrase and explicitly names Jews in the leaving construction, whereas N1904 has a personal pronoun and no synagogue/Jews nouns. The differing named clause material remains a whole source-witness gap.
The pinned TR explicitly names the nations as the appealing subject; N1904 has an understood plural subject without this named group.

13:43.sourceText: λυθείσης δὲ τῆς συναγωγῆς ἠκολούθησαν πολλοὶ τῶν Ἰουδαίων καὶ τῶν σεβομένων προσηλύτων τῷ Παύλῳ καὶ τῷ Βαρνάβᾳ, οἵτινες προσλαλοῦντες αὐτοῖς ἔπειθον αὐτοὺς προσμένειν τῇ χάριτι τοῦ Θεοῦ.
13:43.targetText: and the synagogue having been dismissed, many of the Jews and of the devout proselytes followed Paul and Barnabas, who, speaking to them, were persuading them to remain in the grace of God.

groups.note: The actual σεβομένων is a present worshipping nonactive participle, rendered adjectivally devout; the source remains the worshipping verb, not a separately printed devout adjective.

unmappedSource.reason: The articles before Paul and Barnabas are not separately expressed.

13:44.sourceText: Τῷ δὲ ἐρχομένῳ σαββάτῳ σχεδὸν πᾶσα ἡ πόλις συνήχθη ἀκοῦσαι τὸν λόγον τοῦ Θεοῦ.
13:44.targetText: And on the coming Sabbath, almost all the city was gathered together to hear the word of God,

13:45.sourceText: ἰδόντες δὲ οἱ Ἰουδαῖοι τοὺς ὄχλους ἐπλήσθησαν ζήλου, καὶ ἀντέλεγον τοῖς ὑπὸ Παύλου λαλουμένοις βλασφημοῦντες.
13:45.targetText: and the Jews having seen the multitudes, were filled with zeal, and contradicted the things spoken by Paul—contradicting and slandering.

groups.note: The actual finite ἀντέλεγον names the same immediate continuing contradiction restated in English as contradicted ... contradicting. One actual predicate owns both English repetitions; the pinned TR independently writes an additional ἀντιλέγοντες participle absent from N1904, which is not invented as a second source identity.
The actual λαλουμένοις is a present passive participle of λαλέω, rendered spoken; the pinned TR uses a related saying participle, without replacing this actual N1904 head.

unmappedTarget.reason: The pinned TR has an additional coordinator between its extra contradicting participle and slandering; that coordinator is absent from pinned N1904.

13:46.sourceText: παρρησιασάμενοί τε ὁ Παῦλος καὶ ὁ Βαρνάβας εἶπαν Ὑμῖν ἦν ἀναγκαῖον πρῶτον λαληθῆναι τὸν λόγον τοῦ Θεοῦ· ἐπειδὴ ἀπωθεῖσθε αὐτὸν καὶ οὐκ ἀξίους κρίνετε ἑαυτοὺς τῆς αἰωνίου ζωῆς, ἰδοὺ στρεφόμεθα εἰς τὰ ἔθνη.
13:46.targetText: And speaking boldly, Paul and Barnabas said, “It was necessary that the word of God be first spoken to you, and seeing you thrust it away, and do not judge yourselves worthy of the continuous life, behold, we turn to the nations;

groups.note: The actual bold-speaking participle is aorist, rendered English speaking boldly; its source form is not changed to a present participle.
The actual passive speaking infinitive is rendered as an English that ... be spoken content clause; there is no separate Greek that marker before the word.
The actual ἐπειδή is a since/because conjunction, rendered and seeing as the English causal frame; seeing is not a separately written Greek perception verb.
The actual αἰώνιος adjective is rendered continuous by this translation; its Greek lemma remains the age-lasting/eternal adjective.

unmappedSource.reason: The articles before Paul and Barnabas are not separately expressed.

13:47.sourceText: οὕτως γὰρ ἐντέταλται ἡμῖν ὁ Κύριος Τέθεικά σε εἰς φῶς ἐθνῶν τοῦ εἶναί σε εἰς σωτηρίαν ἕως ἐσχάτου τῆς γῆς.
13:47.targetText: for so the LORD has commanded us: I have set you for a light of nations—for your being for salvation to the end of the earth.”

groups.note: The actual article and being infinitive form the articular-infinitive purpose construction, expressed for ... being; the article does not independently own a bare English for without its verbal head.
The actual accusative σε is the personal subject of the being infinitive, rendered possessive your before the English verbal noun being; the source is not a genitive pronoun.
The actual ἐσχάτου is a substantival farthest/end adjective, rendered the end. No independent Greek τέλος noun is printed.

13:48.sourceText: ἀκούοντα δὲ τὰ ἔθνη ἔχαιρον καὶ ἐδόξαζον τὸν λόγον τοῦ Κυρίου, καὶ ἐπίστευσαν ὅσοι ἦσαν τεταγμένοι εἰς ζωὴν αἰώνιον·
13:48.targetText: And the nations hearing were glad, and were glorifying the word of the LORD, and believed—as many as were appointed to continuous life;

13:49.sourceText: διεφέρετο δὲ ὁ λόγος τοῦ Κυρίου δι’ ὅλης τῆς χώρας.
13:49.targetText: and the word of the LORD was spread abroad through all the region.

13:50.sourceText: οἱ δὲ Ἰουδαῖοι παρώτρυναν τὰς σεβομένας γυναῖκας τὰς εὐσχήμονας καὶ τοὺς πρώτους τῆς πόλεως, καὶ ἐπήγειραν διωγμὸν ἐπὶ τὸν Παῦλον καὶ Βαρνάβαν, καὶ ἐξέβαλον αὐτοὺς ἀπὸ τῶν ὁρίων αὐτῶν.
13:50.targetText: And the Jews stirred up the devout and honorable women, and the first men of the city, and raised persecution against Paul and Barnabas, and put them out from their borders;

groups.note: The actual devout word is a worshipping nonactive participle, not a separately printed pious adjective.
The actual πρώτους is substantival first or leading ones, expanded first men without a separately printed Greek man noun.

unmappedSource.reason: The repeated women-modifier article, the article before Paul, and the article under their borders are not separately expressed.

unmappedTarget.reason: The pinned TR has an additional καί between devout and honorable, absent from N1904.

13:51.sourceText: οἱ δὲ ἐκτιναξάμενοι τὸν κονιορτὸν τῶν ποδῶν ἐπ’ αὐτοὺς ἦλθον εἰς Ἰκόνιον,
13:51.targetText: and having shaken off the dust of their feet against them, they came to Iconium,

groups.note: The actual definite feet are the feet of the shaking agents, rendered their feet. English makes the same agent-owned body-part possession explicit; N1904 has no independent possessive pronoun here, whereas the pinned TR prints an additional αὐτῶν.

unmappedSource.reason: The nominalizing article identifying the shaking people is not separately rendered as those in English; the action has an understood plural subject.

13:52.sourceText: οἵ τε μαθηταὶ ἐπληροῦντο χαρᾶς καὶ Πνεύματος Ἁγίου.
13:52.targetText: and the disciples were filled with joy and the Holy Spirit.

groups.note: The actual genitive joy noun gives the filling content, rendered with joy; no independent Greek with preposition is printed.
